parallel.requirements: Recognized pure Rust 2021, same CLI behavior via std::env::args, byte-for-byte stdout, zero external crates, Cargo project in /output, root test5.rs, and black-box inference from the provided executable.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Started under swarm mode but kept ownership in the main agent after deciding the task was compact and a swarm would risk conflicting edits on the same small set of files.
parallel.implementation: Probed URL parser behavior, inferred fragment and query ordering, scheme and authority handling, userinfo stripping, host and port parsing, then wrote Cargo.toml, test5.rs, and url_parser/mod.rs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integrated the parser directly with the root entry point and produced both the root test5 executable and the Cargo release binary in the expected /output tree.
parallel.verification: Ran rustc and cargo build, then checked about 80 curated differential cases, no-argument exit behavior, and 500 randomized fuzz inputs against the C++ executable with zero mismatches.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished task work was visible at closure; official evaluation completed and passed all 40 testcases.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same pure Rust, no-crates, command-line, byte-for-byte output, Cargo project, root test5.rs, and black-box executable requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Worked as a single serial main agent, probing the executable first and then implementing, testing, repairing, and finalizing the project itself.
serial.implementation: Built a Cargo project with test5.rs and src/url_parser.rs, implemented the same parser behavior, encountered invalid Rust byte escapes for vertical tab and form feed, and edited them to hex escapes.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Delivered a library-backed Cargo project plus the required root entry file and compiled executables, with artifact validation listing the expected entry and release output.
serial.verification: Ran cargo test, cargo build --release, direct rustc compilation, a Perl differential suite over 1640 URL cases plus argument handling, final artifact listing, sample output comparison, and locked release build.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished task work was visible at closure after the byte-escape repair; official evaluation completed and passed all 40 testcases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel-labeled run followed the prompt's Rust 2021, std-only, CLI, output, Cargo layout, root test5.rs, and black-box requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run followed the same prompt requirements and used the same reference executable for black-box behavior inference.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference is visible; both delivered acceptable Rust projects for the same prompt.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Although swarm mode was active, the main agent explicitly kept the compact implementation local and did not spawn or assign child work.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial main agent owned the entire probe, implementation, repair, verification, and finalization sequence itself.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both were effectively single-agent attempts; the parallel run's only decomposition distinction is the explicit decision not to use the available swarm.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: There were no child briefs, child handoffs, or cross-agent interface contracts; the only interface was the local module used by test5.rs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were likewise no child briefs or handoffs; the serial run kept the parser interface inside the main-agent implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No cross-agent context transfer or interface mismatch can be compared because neither trajectory delegated work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel-labeled run wrote a root Cargo.toml, url_parser/mod.rs, and root test5.rs after a focused probe sequence.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run wrote Cargo.toml, root test5.rs, and src/url_parser.rs after broader probing and then patched a byte-escape compile error.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented the same behavior, but the serial path included a compile-error repair while the parallel path compiled on its first build attempt.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: There were no child results to await, retrieve, inspect, merge, or lose; protocol validation reports no delegation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no delegated results in the serial control, and protocol validation likewise reports no delegation or subagents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No result-lifecycle coordination difference exists; all results were local tool outputs consumed by the main agent in each mode.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The main agent made the final project writes itself and artifact validation lists the expected Cargo files, root entry, parser module, and release binary.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial main agent made the final project writes itself and artifact validation lists the expected Cargo files, root entry, source module, and release binary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No shared-workspace race, overwrite, or cross-agent provenance issue occurred because each mode had one writer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel-labeled run compiled with rustc and Cargo, matched 80 curated cases plus no-arg behavior, and then matched 500 fuzz cases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run compiled after repair, matched 1640 URL cases plus argument handling, checked artifact existence and sample output, and rebuilt with --locked.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial verification was broader and included a repaired build failure; both gathered enough evidence before closure and both official evaluations passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel-labeled run completed in one main-agent turn without timeout, with no child work pending, and closed after successful local checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run took longer and used more tool calls, but also completed in one main-agent turn without timeout and closed after successful checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The serial run spent more budget on probing and validation; neither budget profile created unfinished work or an outcome difference.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome. The current completed cell/status.json evaluation for the parallel-labeled run reports 40 passed of 40 evaluated testcases, and the current completed serial evaluation reports the same 40 of 40 result. The process difference is that the parallel-labeled run entered swarm mode but then implemented directly with a shorter probe-and-test cycle, while the serial run probed and tested more extensively and repaired one compile error before final delivery.
parallel_contributors: Direct main-agent implementation after an explicit no-swarm-needed decision.
Focused executable probing followed by successful rustc, Cargo, curated differential, and fuzz checks.
serial_contributors: Broader executable probing and a library-backed Cargo layout.
Compile failure repair followed by a 1640-case Perl differential suite and final artifact checks.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The serial implementation initially used unsupported Rust byte escapes and corrected them before final verification.
The two accepted solutions organized the parser module differently but both satisfied the required root entry and Cargo project layout.
